chunks: And from him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:
I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the Hoopoe, and killing it and slaughtering it, so he said: 'It is not harmed and it is not slaughtered, for it is a good bird.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing or slaughtering the Hoopoe bird in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the status of the Hoopoe bird, noting it is neither harmed nor slaughtered, which implies its meat is permissible (*halal*) and it is not among the birds of prey that are typically prohibited. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the Hoopoe from other birds based on its specific characteristics and behavior, affirming its status as a 'good bird' (*ni'ma al-tayr*). The reference to Surah An-Naml (27:20) in the existing text highlights the bird's narrative role in Prophet Sulayman's court, while this hadith provides the legal (*fiqh*) dimension of its permissibility.
